physics_goals.quote: The first measurement of the P2 experiment aims for a high precision determination of the weak mixing angle to a precision of 0.14%
physics_goals.value: Determine the weak mixing angle to a precision of 0.14% at low four-momentum transfer through parity-violating electron-proton scattering

summary.plain: P2 will measure the weak mixing angle, a basic number of the Standard Model, with unprecedented precision at low energy by scattering spin-polarised electrons from the new MESA accelerator in Mainz off hydrogen and measuring the tiny parity-violating asymmetry.
summary.technical: P2 experiment at MESA: parity-violating elastic electron-proton scattering of 155 MeV longitudinally polarised electrons at Q^2 = 4.5e-3 GeV^2 on a liquid-hydrogen target with a solenoid spectrometer of full azimuthal acceptance and Cherenkov detectors, aiming at the weak mixing angle to 0.14% (the weak charge of the proton to about 2%); also neutron skin of 208Pb and two-photon-exchange asymmetries.
